title: Recording Music Goes Round and Round with Froeberg
summary: He made the record with Froeberg and Berrigan on December 24, 1935, and was given the bridge solo.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: It'll be a great day in the morning? Oh, yeah. You know that, huh? Oh, yeah. You know the tune called Music Goes Round and Round? Oh, yeah, I should.
Why? I made a record on that one. Oh, really?
It was Froben, yeah. So Froben, who was in the band?

I wanted Berrigan, Froben, and I'll tell you the truth, I can't remember who else. It was one of them dates. It was kind of foggy. I don't know. I know Berrigan was on it, I know that. I knew we were a little disappointed because it didn't come out as good as we wanted it to come out. You know, didn't think it was good to be on it.
That's the one you told me you took a solo one?
Yeah, they gave me the bridge on it. I never did much of that kind of stuff.
What about these tunes, Just Naturally Lazy? Just Naturally Lazy, do you know that?

I remember, it seems like I remember the title of that, actually. If I heard the tune it might come back to me too. Take it along with you? A lot of tunes, I don't know them by name, I'll tell you. I never did bother with words or the melody. It's stuck in my mind more. Ain't nobody's business what I do?
Yeah. If I could sing I'd sing it for you, but I can't sing.
I know, I think if I hear it I'd know it.
Just me and Caroline, tagging along with you and just Natural Relations.
Those are some of Freiber's numbers. I didn't know if you made one session or two with him or what?
We just made that two sides, that one side I can recall. What was on the other side? We must have made the other side too. What's on the other side?
It should be Just Naturally Lazy or there'll be a great day in the morning.

I think it was a great day, I think. I've got a better recollection of that. Must have been a great day. I can't remember. Remember we made the day, it didn't mean much to anybody. I mean we just made it and forgot about it. You know what I mean? I don't know, one of those things.
Yeah that was December 24th, 1935. It was? The day before Christmas. Yeah.
I don't know if Christmas meant much in 35 to a lot of people. There's no Santa Claus maybe.
